title: Ecological Roles of Microorganisms
description: Flip each card to reveal the definition and a clinical example.

dialogs.answer: Benefit the host or are neutral; cause no disease under normal conditions. Example: viridans streptococci in the oral cavity.

tips.front: Think 'eating at the same table' — sharing space without harm.

dialogs.answer: Both host and microbe benefit from the relationship. Example: E. coli in the colon synthesises Vitamin K for the host.

tips.front: Both partners gain something from the relationship.

dialogs.answer: Harmless in healthy hosts but pathogenic when host defences are compromised. Example: Candida albicans in immunocompromised patients.

tips.front: They wait for an 'opportunity' — a break in host defences.

dialogs.answer: Always capable of causing disease in a normal host through virulence factors. Example: Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

tips.front: These organisms do not need host compromise to cause disease.
